Finite Brownian coordinate type J; filtered Brownian setup; scalar integrands eta_j; row Y=∑_j I_j(eta_j); dyadic quadratic-variation error E_n.

Omega is measurable with finite measure mu and a filtration F indexed by nonnegative reals. T>0 is fixed. The Euclidean coordinate type J is finite with decidable equality. B:[0,infinity)×Omega→R^J. lambda_T denotes the pullback under NNReal.toReal of Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,T]. eta:J→progressive L² integrands.

Assumptions: B starts at zero for every omega, has jointly independent increments over disjoint half-open intervals, every continuous real linear functional ell sends B_t-B_s (s<t) to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||², and paths are continuous mu-a.e. B is strongly adapted to F and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. A progressive L² integrand is a real process a(t,omega), strongly progressive for F, for which (omega,t)↦a(t,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). No fourth-moment or boundedness assumption on eta is imposed.

Conclusion: I_j(a)(t,omega) denotes the specified completed Ito integral driven by the scalar coordinate B^j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j. Its representative is the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic integrals off the null complement of their uniform Cauchy event, and zero on that complement; it is held constant after T. Put t_i^n=iT/2^n and Y(t)=∑_j I_j(eta_j)(t). Define E_n=∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}(Y(t_{i+1}^n)-Y(t_i^n))²-∑_j∫eta_j(s)²d lambda_T(s). Then E_n is mu-integrable for every n and ∫|E_n|dmu→0 as n→infinity.

Quantifier order: For every listed setup and family eta, every dyadic error E_n is integrable and its absolute first moment tends to zero.

Scope: L¹ convergence of quadratic-variation errors at one positive horizon; neither L² membership of errors nor a.s. convergence is asserted. The integrands are fixed as n varies.

Constant dependencies: No numerical constant or rate is introduced.
